user.title: AI models
user.description: First look checks every sighting. Second opinion double-checks the unsure and important ones; without it, priority animals, look-alikes and new animals are never confirmed. To get a second model, add another AI Task with a different model in your AI integration (its page → Add AI task). If a model is busy, failing or out of its free daily allowance (quota), the next one in its list is tried.

data_description.first_look: Runs on every sighting, tried in order. Tip: put the cheapest model with the biggest free allowance first (e.g. Flash-Lite), backups after it.
data_description.second_opinion: Looks again at unsure answers, unknown animals, priority and Always strict animals, wild animals like raccoons or foxes, and any animal a backup model named. Tip: put a smarter model first, and don't reuse First look's models.

schedule.title: When to watch
schedule.description: Cameras are checked between Watch from and Watch until. Also watch whenever it is dark adds the hours the sun is down. Watch all day ignores both and checks around the clock (uses more AI quota).

data.use_dark: Also watch whenever it is dark

data_description.use_dark: Adds the hours between sunset and sunrise.
data_description.watch_always: For daytime visitors too. Every check uses AI quota, so this uses more.

more.name: More
more.description: When the night summary is built, and how long an animal shows as on camera.

data_description.summary_time: Last night's summary is built at this time each morning, and a new night starts. Set it just after Watch until.
data_description.on_camera_minutes: How long an animal shows as on camera after a sighting.

cameras.title: Cameras
cameras.description: Pick the cameras to watch. Each one is set up on the next pages, filled in from its own device. You can add more later under Configure → Cameras.

camera.title: Camera: {camera}
camera.description: We filled this in from the camera's own device: motion and animal sensors start a check, person and vehicle sensors skip one. Make sure they're right.{sensors}

data.name: Name
data.triggers: Start a check when any of these turn on
data.skip_when: Skip the check while any of these are on

data_description.name: Used in the AI prompt, alerts and the summary, e.g. Garage.
data_description.ai_notes: Only this camera's checks see it. E.g. the bins are at the left; a cat behind the window on the right is an indoor pet. Notes you add while reviewing a sighting are added here too.
data_description.skip: Picked by mistake? Turn this on and submit to leave it out.
data_description.triggers: The camera's motion or animal sensors. A check runs each time one turns on, during the hours set under When to watch.
data_description.skip_when: For example its person or vehicle sensor, so people and cars don't use AI quota. Checks you start by hand (the Identify action) ignore this.

timing.name: Timing
timing.description: How often this camera is checked.

data.reopened_by: A check on these cameras ends the cooldown

data_description.cooldown: Shortest time between two checks of this camera.
data_description.reopened_by: Cameras an animal passes on its way here (e.g. a gate before the porch). Once one of them is checked, this camera can be checked again straight away. Only cameras set up before this one are listed; add the others later under Configure → Cameras.
data_description.check_every: For a camera with no motion sensor: check it on a timer, during watch hours only. 0 = only when a sensor turns on. Every check uses AI quota. The Cooldown still applies.

deterrent.name: Scaring pests off
deterrent.description: Lights and a sound for when a pest is seen here.

data.deterrent_lights: Lights or switches that scare pests off

data_description.deterrent_lights: Turned on when a pest is seen here, then back off.
data_description.deterrent_minutes: How long they stay on after the last pest sighting.
data_description.deterrent_sound: Played when a pest is seen here.

animal.title: Animals

data_description.species: Pick one or type any other kind.
data_description.description: Sent to the AI. The most important field: lead with markings that still show at night in infrared (white paws, bib, tail rings, size).
data_description.reference_upload: A clear night photo, sent to the AI beside each frame.
data_description.sprite: Cats only. How the card draws it when there's no recent photo. Doesn't affect recognition.

looks.name: Card picture and tips
looks.description: Extra tips for the AI, and a custom card picture.

data_description.tips: Also sent to the AI, right after What it looks like: what it's confused with, how to tell them apart. Notes you add after correcting a sighting are added here too.
data_description.appearance:
Optional, for tinkerers. Changes the picked picture, one setting per line. Example:
fur: "#7f7e7b"
tabby: true
whitePaws: true
collar: "#3f9a55"
Leave empty if the picture above is close enough.

rules.name: Alerts and strictness
rules.description: How carefully it is checked, and where it alerts.

data_description.priority: The animal you'd hate to miss, e.g. a pet that goes outside. It always gets a second look, it's only confirmed when both AI models agree and see its coat, and it gets a Confirmed on camera sensor. Needs a Second opinion model (Configure → AI models); without one it is never confirmed.
data_description.pattern: Priority animals only. Both AI models must report this pattern before it's confirmed. Leave Don't check if unsure: a wrong pick means it is never confirmed.
data_description.base: Priority animals only. The tone covering more than half the body; small white paws, a chest or a bib don't make it White. Infrared shows tones, not colours (a ginger cat often looks grey). Leave Don't check if unsure.
data_description.always_strict: For an animal that's easy to mix up with another (e.g. a neighbour's look-alike): it only counts when both AI models are sure it's this one. Animals not seen for a while, and new ones until they're first confirmed, get this automatically. Ignored for a priority animal, which is already checked more strictly. Needs a Second opinion model (Configure → AI models); without one it is never confirmed.
data_description.alert_at: Cameras where it alerts phones. Empty: no alerts (it's still tracked).
data_description.critical_at: Critical alerts ring through silent mode. Only while this animal's Critical alerts switch (at the top of its page on the Neighborhood Watch sidebar page, or on its device; it starts off) is on. Empty: every camera in Alert at. Picking a camera here also alerts there. iPhone: allow Critical Alerts for the Home Assistant app in iOS Settings → Notifications.

last_seen.name: Last seen
last_seen.description: A new animal only counts once both AI models are sure it's this one. If it already visits, enter roughly when you last saw it, so it counts normally from the start.

data_description.known_last_seen: Roughly. Clear this for an animal that has never visited.

wildlife.title: Pests
wildlife.description: Which animals are pests? Pests alert every time they come back and can be scared off with a camera's lights and sound. Every other animal is still recognised and tracked as wildlife, with no setup.

data_description.pests: Pick from the list or type any animal.

people.title: Who gets alerts
people.description: These phones get Neighborhood Watch alerts, including missing-mode alerts (when you mark a lost pet as missing, every possible sighting rings). Each person's mutes, quiet zones and hours, and critical sound can be changed later under Configure → People.

data_description.phones: Phones with the Home Assistant app. All are ticked; untick any that shouldn't get alerts.

error.first_look_required: Pick at least one model for the first look.
error.name_taken: That name is already used (names differing only in capitals or punctuation count as the same). Pick another.
error.name_reserved: That name is used by Neighborhood Watch itself (Unknown…, None, Nothing, Pests, Other wildlife, Unknown animals, Unsure motion). Pick another.
error.photo_unreadable: That photo can't be read. Use a JPEG, PNG or iPhone (HEIC) photo.
error.name_letters: Use at least one letter or number in the name.
error.sprite_cats_only: Card pictures are cats only. Clear Picture on the card and Advanced: custom card picture, or set Species to Cat.
error.appearance_not_settings: Use setting: value lines, e.g. fur: "#d0813f" and tabby: true. Leave it empty to use the picture picked above.
error.needs_second_opinion: Priority and Always strict need a Second opinion model. Add one under Configure → AI models, or turn these off.
error.same_model: Pick different models for Second opinion: a model rarely disagrees with itself.

abort.no_ai_task: Set up an AI integration with an AI Task that can read images first (for example Google Generative AI), then add Neighborhood Watch again.

init.title: Neighborhood Watch
init.description: Animals are on the integration page: Add animal adds one, and each animal's ⋮ menu has Edit animal. Each animal's switches (Alerts, Critical alerts, Missing mode) are on its device page and on the Neighborhood Watch sidebar page.

advanced.description: Settings most people never need to change.

identification.title: AI instructions
identification.description: What the AI is told on every check. Most people only need the notes and visitors below. If you edit the instructions, keep the words in braces: {animals} (required: your animals' descriptions), {location} (the camera's name), {absent}, {extra_rules} (the notes below), {wildlife} and {unknown_kinds}.

data.reset_instructions: Discard my edits and restore the default instructions

data_description.extra_rules: Rules for every camera. Notes about one camera go on that camera's page.
data_description.wildlife: Animals you often see, as hints. Not a limit: the AI names whatever it sees, and corrections accept any animal.
data_description.reference_photos: Each animal's reference photo goes to the AI beside the frame. More accurate; each check costs a little more of your AI allowance.
data_description.absent_days: An animal not seen this long, or a new one until it's first confirmed, is named only when both AI models are sure. Needs a Second opinion model.

notifications.title: Pictures in alerts
notifications.description: Alerts carry a picture that phones open. Leave this empty if pictures already load away from home (Home Assistant Cloud, or an Internet address under Settings → System → Network). Fill it in only if they don't.

data_description.public_url: The address phones reach this Home Assistant at from outside, e.g. {example}.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.description: Where alerts go is set on each animal, and for everything else under Pests and Other animals and motion. Who gets them, and their quiet times, is set under People.

data.correction_buttons: Right / Not sure / Other buttons on alerts
data.review_page: Page that opens when you tap an alert

data_description.alerts: Turn off if your own automations send the alerts (they can use the sighting event).
data_description.correction_buttons: Tap to confirm or correct a sighting. Corrections fix tracking and are saved with the photo.
data_description.review_page: e.g. /neighborhood-watch#review (the sidebar page, admins only) or a dashboard with the card, e.g. /lovelace/pets#review. Empty = the app opens as usual.
data_description.min_confidence: Medium is a good start. Less sure answers don't alert; they wait in To review. Critical alerts, unsure motion and missing mode ignore this.

training.title: Saved photos
training.description: Every checked frame is saved (downscaled, unless full size is on) with what the AI said and what you answered. These photos are shown in To review, used when you correct a sighting, and are what the local detector trains on.

data_description.dataset_dir: Leave empty for the media folder. For a network share added under Settings → System → Storage, enter its path, e.g. /media/your_share/neighborhood_watch. Existing photos stay where they are; use the Move saved photos action to bring them over. The local detector trains on this folder: mount it into the vision service at /dataset.
data_description.dataset_gb: When full, the oldest unanswered photos go first; ones you answered are kept longest.
data_description.dataset_full_size: Off: photos are shrunk to 1280 pixels wide. On: they keep the camera's size (up to 4K), so the local detector trains on animals as large as it sees them live and finds small ones better. Takes about 4 times the space, so the oldest unanswered photos are removed sooner: raise Keep at most to match. Applies to photos saved from now on.

detector.title: Local detector
detector.description: Optional. A free detector on your own NAS or PC that looks at every photo before the AI. It trains on your answers in To review (on a schedule, or after every so many answers), and learns to name each animal you've answered often enough, so the AI is needed less and less. Start in Test only. Once the Detector tab shows 0 missed animals, switch to Skip empty frames.

data.detector_min: How sure the detector must be (0 to 1)

data_description.detector_url: e.g. {example}. Leave empty to turn it off.
data_description.detector_min: Below this the photo counts as empty. Lower catches more animals but skips fewer empty frames. 0.2 is a good start; lower it if the Detector agreement sensor shows misses.
data_description.local_naming: Trust it first: a name it has proved it gets right (95% of the time on photos it didn't train on) is used without asking the AI. Priority, always-strict, long-absent and missing animals still go to the AI. The Detector tab shows which names it can be trusted with.

catch_alls.title: Other animals and motion
catch_alls.description: Every animal is recognised and tracked without adding it. Here you set where the rest alert. Each group's critical alerts switch is on the sidebar page's Animals tab, or on the Neighborhood Watch device.

unknown.name: Unknown animals
unknown.description: A cat or dog that isn't one of yours.

data_description.unknown_alert_at: All cameras includes cameras added later. To leave one out, remove All cameras and pick the others. Empty: never.
data_description.unknown_critical_at: Critical alerts ring through silent mode. Only while the Unknown animals critical alerts switch (on the sidebar page's Animals tab, or on the Neighborhood Watch device; it starts off) is on. Empty: every camera in Alert at. Picking a camera here also alerts there.

other.name: Other wildlife
other.description: Any wild animal that isn't a pest. Birds, chickens, chipmunks, deer, groundhogs and squirrels never alert; they're still tracked.

data_description.other_alert_at: All cameras includes cameras added later. To leave one out, remove All cameras and pick the others. Empty: never.
data_description.other_critical_at: Critical alerts ring through silent mode. Only while the Other wildlife critical alerts switch (on the sidebar page's Animals tab, or on the Neighborhood Watch device; it starts off) is on. Empty: every camera in Alert at. Picking a camera here also alerts there.

motion.name: Unsure motion
motion.description: The AI saw movement but couldn't say what.

data_description.motion_alert_at: All cameras includes cameras added later. To leave one out, remove All cameras and pick the others. Empty: never.
data_description.motion_critical_at: Critical alerts ring through silent mode. Only while the Unsure motion critical alerts switch (on the sidebar page's Animals tab, or on the Neighborhood Watch device; it starts off) is on. Empty: every camera in Alert at. Picking a camera here also alerts there.

critical_alerts.description: What rings through silent mode here.

data.critical_except: Never ring through silent mode here for

data_description.critical_except: While this camera's Critical alerts for anything here switch is on (on the camera's device, or at the top of its page in the sidebar; it starts off), everything seen here rings through silent mode, even unsure motion and animals whose alerts are off. List what should never ring here, e.g. a pet that sleeps in the garage. People's mutes still apply.

person.title: Person

data_description.person: Optional. Used only to know where they are, for quiet zones.
data_description.notify_service: Usually the phone with the Home Assistant app. Other notify services get the alert as text with a link to the picture: no critical sound, no buttons.
data_description.remove: Turn on, then Submit, to delete this person. They stop getting alerts and their critical-alerts switch goes too. Other changes on this page are not saved.

critical_alerts.name: Missing mode and critical sound
critical_alerts.description: Missing-mode alerts, and how critical alerts sound. To make all of this person's alerts normal ones, turn off their '… gets critical alerts' switch (on their phone's device, or at the top of their page in the sidebar).

data_description.missing_alerts: They get the critical alert for any possible sighting of an animal in Missing mode, instead of the normal one.
data_description.critical_sound: A sound file name from the iPhone Companion app, or default. Android ignores this. iPhone: allow Critical Alerts for the Home Assistant app in iOS Settings → Notifications.
data_description.critical_volume: From 0.1 to 1 (full volume). Missing-mode alerts always ring at full volume.

mutes.name: Mutes
mutes.description: Animals this person never hears about.

data_description.muted: This person gets no alerts for these, critical ones included. If Gets missing-mode alerts is on, missing-mode alerts still reach them.

quiet.name: Quiet zones and hours
quiet.description: Where and when alerts stop ringing through silent mode, or stop altogether.

data.quiet_mode: When in a quiet zone or quiet hours

data_description.quiet_zones: Zones (like work) where the setting below applies. Needs Their Home Assistant person above.
data_description.quiet_start: Optional: a daily window, like overnight.
data_description.quiet_end: Leave both empty for no quiet hours.
data_description.quiet_mode: Missing-mode alerts always arrive, at most as normal ones.

pests.title: Pests
pests.description: Pests are animals you want gone, like a raccoon at the bins. By default they alert at every camera, every time they come back, and set off a camera's lights and sound (Cameras → Scaring pests off). Any animal not listed is other wildlife. These settings apply to all pests together. The Pests critical alerts switch is on the sidebar page's Animals tab, or on the Neighborhood Watch device.

data_description.pests: Pick from the list or type any animal.
data_description.pest_alert_at: All cameras includes cameras added later. To leave one out, remove All cameras and pick the others. Empty: never.
data_description.pest_critical_at: Critical alerts ring through silent mode. Only while the Pests critical alerts switch (on the sidebar page's Animals tab, or on the Neighborhood Watch device; it starts off) is on. Empty: every camera in Alert at. Picking a camera here also alerts there.

error.person_needed: Pick Their Home Assistant person to use quiet zones.
error.folder_not_absolute: Enter the full path, starting with /, e.g. /media/your_share/neighborhood_watch.
error.folder_unwritable: That folder can't be created or written to. Check the path and that the share is connected.
error.camera_taken: That camera is already set up. Pick it from the Cameras list to change it.
error.quiet_hours_both: Set both Quiet hours start and end (different times), or leave both empty.
error.notify_unknown: No notify service by that name. Pick one from the list.
error.same_model: Pick different models for Second opinion: a model rarely disagrees with itself.
error.detector_unreachable: Couldn't reach the detector at that address. Check it's running and the address (including http:// and the port) is right.

error.name_reserved: That name is used by Neighborhood Watch itself (Unknown…, None, Nothing, Pests, Other wildlife, Unknown animals, Unsure motion). Pick another.
error.photo_unreadable: That photo can't be read. Use a JPEG, PNG or iPhone (HEIC) photo.
error.name_letters: Use at least one letter or number in the name.
error.sprite_cats_only: Card pictures are cats only. Clear Picture on the card and Advanced: custom card picture, or set Species to Cat.
error.appearance_not_settings: Use setting: value lines, e.g. fur: "#d0813f" and tabby: true. Leave it empty to use the picture picked above.
error.needs_second_opinion: Priority and Always strict need a Second opinion model. Add one under Configure → AI models, or turn these off.

options.shadow: Test only: ask the detector and compare with the AI, change nothing
options.skip_empty: Skip empty frames: no AI check when the detector sees no animal (never in missing mode)

options.normal: Critical alerts arrive as normal ones

options.calico_collar: Calico with a collar and bell
options.grey_chest_spot: Grey with a white chest spot
options.longhair_tuxedo: Long-haired tuxedo with one white leg
options.charcoal_white_chest: Charcoal with a white chest and back feet
options.smoky_banded_tail: Smoky tabby with a banded tail
options.bicolour_mask_paw_up: Black and white, lopsided mask, often a paw up

options.first: Trust it first: no AI call for names it has proved it gets right
options.fill_in: Only when no AI model answers

snapshot_failed.message: The snapshot from {camera} failed; see the log.

no_photo.message: There is no photo of that animal yet; name a camera to take one now.

note_needs_target.message: Choose a camera or an animal for the note.

no_detector.message: Set the local detector's address under Configure → Advanced → Local detector first.

identify.name: Identify
identify.description: Checks a camera now, ignoring its cooldown, and returns what the AI found.

test_sighting.name: Test sighting
test_sighting.description: Fires a fake sighting event marked test, so you can check your alerts. Tracking is never changed.

priority_candidate.name: Priority candidate
priority_candidate.description: Whether either AI named a priority animal. Auto = yes only when the animal is one.

mark_wrong.name: Mark wrong
mark_wrong.description: Removes an animal's latest counted sighting from tracking, e.g. when it was really another animal.

animal.name: Animal
animal.description: The animal that was named wrongly.

camera.name: Camera
camera.description: Only the latest sighting at this camera.

set_reference_photo.name: Set reference photo
set_reference_photo.description: Uses the animal's last photo as its reference photo, or takes one from a camera now.

camera.name: Camera
camera.description: Take a fresh snapshot from this camera instead.

build_summary.name: Build night summary
build_summary.description: Builds the night summary now and starts a new night.

undo_last_answer.name: Undo the last answer
undo_last_answer.description: Takes back the last Right / Not sure / Other / It was… answer: the sighting goes back to To review, and tracking and the photo follow.

correct.name: Correct a sighting
correct.description: Confirms or corrects what a camera saw. Tracking and the photo move to the right animal, and the saved photo is labelled.

answer.name: Answer
answer.description: right, wrong, unsure (looked at, no verdict), or what it really was (an animal's name, a wildlife kind, or nothing).

sighting_id.name: Sighting
sighting_id.description: The sighting's id (from an alert or Last detection). Empty = the latest one.

camera.name: Camera
camera.description: Without an id: the latest sighting at this camera.

scan.name: Scan a folder
scan.description: Bulk-scans photos and videos in a folder on the local detector's machine. The detector finds each animal visit, the AI names it, and a report is written into the folder. Visits also appear in To review.

folder.name: Folder
folder.description: A folder inside the detector's scan folder, e.g. trailcam/2026-10.

identify.name: Name the animals
identify.description: Ask the AI what each visit is (uses AI quota: one or two calls per visit).

limit.name: At most
limit.description: How many visits to name; the rest are listed as "animal".

add_note.name: Add a note for the AI
add_note.description: Adds a note where the AI will use it: a camera's view notes, or an animal's identification tips.

camera.name: Camera
camera.description: Add it to this camera's view notes.

animal.name: Animal
animal.description: Or add it to this animal's (or wildlife kind's) tips.

move_training_data.name: Move saved photos
move_training_data.description: Moves saved photos into the folder set under Saved photos, e.g. after pointing it at a NAS.

from.name: From
from.description: Folders to move from. Empty: the default folder in the media folder.

mark_animal.name: Mark the animal
mark_animal.description: Saves where the animal is in a sighting's photo (the card does this when you drag a box on the enlarged photo). The local detector's training uses your box before any other, and the zoomed-in photo is cut around it.

box.name: Box
box.description: Left, top, right, bottom, each from 0 to 1 of the photo. Empty takes the mark away.

no_second_opinion.title: Neighborhood Watch needs a Second opinion model
no_second_opinion.description: No Second opinion model is set. Without one, priority animals are never confirmed, and an animal marked Always strict or not seen for a while is never counted again. Add a different model under Settings → Devices & services → Neighborhood Watch → Configure → AI models.
